column2: Retain year 160, Alexander son of Antiochus, Epiphanes, Ptolemais and reception as king. The nominative epithet follows Alexander in the selected grammar; do not silently move it onto his genitive father’s name.
Retain Demetrius hearing, gathering very large forces and going to meet Alexander in battle. The purpose is explicit and distinct from his subsequent diplomatic approach.
Retain peaceful letters intended to exalt Jonathan. The expressed aim is not equated with sincere reconciliation, which the following motive qualifies.
Retain urgency to precede Alexander, plural peace partners and singular Jonathan’s possible agreement. The number changes remain visible rather than uniformly naming Jonathan everywhere.
Retain remembrance of all evils committed against Jonathan, brothers and nation. The speaker acknowledges his side’s actions, without a translator-supplied apology.
Retain authority to recruit, prepare weapons and ally, and release of citadel hostages. The permissions and hostage order are separate measures.
Retain public reading before all people and those from the citadel. In the hearing naturally expresses into their ears while preserving the full audience.
Retain great fear at the granted recruiting authority. The unexpressed plural subject is not narrowed by an added official title.
Retain citadel men handing over hostages and Jonathan returning them to their parents. Parents preserves both parental possibilities rather than silently specifying fathers alone.
Retain residence in Jerusalem and beginning to rebuild and renew. Both construction verbs remain without implying the entire project was immediately completed.
Retain workers, walls, Zion and four-foot stones provisionally. Enclosure supplies the contextual construction around the mount, not a second temple mentioned in the source.
column3: What dimension or shape does the four-foot expression describe? The inherited wording does not certify modern feet or a fully established architectural interpretation.

column2: Retain foreigners fleeing the strongholds Bacchides built. The relative clause identifies the fortifications without adding new locations.
Retain each leaving his own post/place and going to his own land. The distributive each must not become an assertion of one shared destination.
Retain the Beth-zur exception, abandonment of law/decrees and refuge function. Only reflects the exceptive opening rather than an unsupported exclusivity.
Retain Alexander hearing promises and receiving reports of Jonathan/brothers’ battles, bravery and hardship. The unnamed reporters and subject transition remain contextual.
Retain the rhetorical question about finding another comparable man and the decision on friendship/alliance. Another is contextual for the uniqueness question, not a separate explicit numeral.
column3: What negative expectation does the question carry? The inherited Could we find another preserves a question but leaves its rhetorical force to context.

column2: Retain writing and sending letters with the following wording. Do not add a named scribe or material.
Retain King Alexander’s greeting to brother Jonathan. Brother is diplomatic address and does not establish biological kinship.
Retain mighty in strength and suitability for royal friendship. Ordinary you addresses a human recipient despite his coming priestly rank.

Retain now/today, high priesthood, king’s Friend, the parenthetical purple robe/golden crown, and attention to royal interests. Keep the narrator’s interruption distinct from the letter’s quoted voice.
Retain holy robe, seventh month, year 160, Booths festival, recruited forces and many weapons. No later ritual description is inserted.
Retain Demetrius hearing and grieving before speech. Grief is not automatically intensified to rage, a different response used elsewhere.
Retain the self-question and Alexander’s having anticipated them in securing Jewish support. The military/political support image remains without making friendship purely private affection.
Retain encouragement, honour and gifts as the proposed letter’s inducements. Honour naturally renders height/exaltation in this diplomatic context.
Retain the greeting to the Jewish nation and the narrator’s introduction. The speaker changes to the royal first-person letter afterward.
Retain the claimed maintained agreements, friendship and nondefection, followed by rejoicing. These claims belong to Demetrius’s letter and are not separately certified by the translator.
Retain continued faithfulness and promised repayment in good things. Faith here is political fidelity, without importing an unrelated doctrinal meaning.
Retain many remissions and gifts as two promised benefits. Remissions remains broad until the fiscal specifications follow.
Retain release from tribute, salt charge and crown payments for all Jews. Crown payments is a contextual fiscal rendering of crowns and remains open to technical clarification.
column3: What precise fiscal institution is denoted by crowns in this letter? No specific taxation mechanism is established by the English alone.

column2: Retain one-third grain and one-half tree-fruit, Judah plus three districts from Samaria/Galilee, and repeated today/perpetuity expressions. The source’s repetitions and proportions are not simplified or reconciled with verse 38.
Retain Jerusalem/territory holy and exempt, with tithes and dues. Free of makes the elliptical exemption relation explicit but remains provisional.
column3: Do the final tithes/dues name remitted charges or revenue assigned with the city? The syntax does not independently settle the fiscal scope.

column2: Retain relinquished citadel authority to the high priest and his choice of guards. His own selection is explicit, not the king choosing each appointee.

Retain every captive Jewish person released without payment, plus remission including livestock. Person naturally expresses soul; the second clause’s all refers to those required to remit, not automatically the captives themselves.
column3: Who must remit the taxes, and whose livestock is covered? Keep the referents provisional pending fiscal and syntactic review.

column2: Retain festivals, sabbaths, new moons, appointed days and three days on each side of a festival. The all/Jews/kingdom scope remains without reducing the exemption to one feast.
Retain no authority to exact payment or trouble anyone about any matter. The universal negatives remain within the preceding remission context.
Retain recruitment of thirty thousand provisionally as up to, and allowances appropriate to royal troops. The Greek numerical preposition does not by itself certify a strict upper limit.
column3: Does the number mean thirty thousand, about thirty thousand or up to that strength? Also review allowances as the technical military-payment term.

column2: Retain fort postings, trusted offices, supervisors from their own group and their own laws. The grammatical transition from singular appointment wording to plural appointees is naturally distributed as some.
Retain the three Samarian districts, repeated attachment to Judea, unified authority and high-priest exception. Do not insert Galilee here solely to harmonize verse 30.
Retain Ptolemais and its attached territory as a gift for Jerusalem’s holy-place expenses. The stated gift is not reduced to an unstated fixed fraction of revenue.
Retain annual fifteen thousand silver shekels, royal accounts and appropriate places. No modern monetary equivalent is supplied.
Retain excess previously unpaid and future allocation to the house’s works. The difficult account/revenue relation remains visible rather than becoming an invented budget formula.
column3: What surplus and prior nonpayment are referred to, and how does as in former years qualify them? Full fiscal interpretation remains pending.

column2: Retain five thousand silver shekels annually remitted because they belong to ministering priests. The earlier taking is plural and not silently made a first-person act by the king.
Retain refuge within the Jerusalem temple/precincts, royal dues or other obligations, and release extending to possessions. The personal/property protection remains broad but provisional.
column3: What debts or proceedings does every matter encompass, and how does the singular owing participle relate to all refugees? No modern asylum rule is inferred.

column2: Retain royal-account payment for building and renewal of holy-place works. The source promises funding, not proof that the funds were disbursed.
Retain Jerusalem walls, encircling fortification, royal-account expense and Judean walls. The final broader wall clause remains distinct from Jerusalem alone.

Retain Jonathan/people neither trusting nor accepting the terms because of remembered great evil and oppression. Both negative responses remain, without replacing their stated reason with conjectured economics.

Propose they fought alongside him continually for they remained his allies all his days. The verb describes allied fighting and the duration says all the days without the inherited possessive limiting it to Alexander’s lifetime. Keep the claim that he initiated peaceful words as the people’s stated rationale.
column3: How literally should all the days be expressed in this narrative summary? Continually is a provisional duration rendering, not proof of an uninterrupted campaign.

column2: Retain Alexander gathering large forces and encamping opposite Demetrius. No battlefield location is supplied.
Retain the two kings’ battle, Demetrius’s army fleeing, Alexander pursuing him and prevailing over them. Singular pursued target and plural defeated group remain distinct.
Retain He pressing battle until sunset and Demetrius falling that day. The unexpressed singular subject of the first verb is deliberately not resolved by inserting a king’s name.
column3: Does the first verb resume Alexander or shift to Demetrius? The inherited He preserves the open subject transition.

column2: Retain envoys to Ptolemy king of Egypt and the introduction of the message. No ordinal or later royal epithet is added.
Retain returned kingdom, fathers’ throne, governmental control, Demetrius defeated and our country. The shift from my to our is present in the selected speech and not flattened.
Retain first-person singular battle followed by plural victory and enthronement on his kingdom’s throne. The royal we remains distinct from the earlier singular claim.

Retain friendship, request for the daughter, son-in-law relation and gifts to father/daughter worthy of the father. The second now in the Greek is not independently represented in the inherited next sentence and remains a closer-draft question.
column3: Should the repeated now be restored before Give me your daughter? The repetition is source-present, though its discourse force is carried by the sequential English request.

column2: Retain Ptolemy’s good-day greeting with return to ancestral land and throne. The English past framing naturally expresses the retrospectively celebrated day without adding a new date.

Retain agreement, meeting at Ptolemais, reciprocal sight and marriage alliance. The same marriage verb need not mean Ptolemy becomes a son-in-law; his reciprocal family relation is contextually different.
Retain Ptolemy and daughter Cleopatra travelling from Egypt to Ptolemais in year 162. This Cleopatra is not identified with a later bearer of that name.
Retain Alexander meeting Ptolemy, the daughter’s marriage and a royal-style glorious wedding. The giving subject shifts contextually to the father without making Cleopatra Alexander’s daughter.
column3: Would naming Ptolemy improve the English pronoun sequence? The current inherited sequence remains provisional because the named father is available in the preceding unit.

column2: Retain Alexander’s written summons to Jonathan. The selected inflected name form does not establish a different person.
Retain Jonathan’s honourable arrival, both kings, gifts to them and their Friends, and finding favour. Court Friends is not silently reduced to the two kings’ private companions.
Retain pestilent men and lawless men as the narrator’s descriptions, their accusation and the king’s refusal to heed. The disease metaphor is not a medical diagnosis.
Retain the king’s order, removal of garments, clothing in purple and execution of the order. The English infinitive construction unfolds the source’s command-plus-action sequence naturally.
Retain seating beside the king, public proclamation and prohibition on any accusation or harassment. The repeated universal protections are not reduced to one pending lawsuit.
Retain accusers seeing proclaimed honour and purple clothing, then all fleeing. The supplied passive as proclaimed leaves the proclamation’s unexpressed singular subject open.
Retain honour, enrollment among First Friends, generalship and district governorship. The court grade remains distinct from ordinary Friends and later Kinsmen.
column3: What exact authority is conveyed by the district-governor title in this setting? The English is a provisional functional rendering, not a modern office equivalence.

column2: Retain return to Jerusalem with peace and gladness. Both the condition of peace and emotional rejoicing remain.
Retain year 165 and Demetrius son of Demetrius coming from Crete. The patronymic distinguishes him from the earlier king without inserting a modern regnal number.
Retain Alexander’s great distress and return to Antioch. Distress is not silently changed to anger.

Retain Demetrius appointing Apollonius, the Coele-Syria role, great force, Jamnia and message to Jonathan the high priest. He in the next sentence contextually resumes Apollonius but remains formally ambiguous.
column3: Does the participle describe an already-held governorship or the appointment’s content? The inherited who was over preserves that distinction provisionally.

column2: Retain emphatic you alone, self-exaltation, ridicule/reproach and challenge over mountain power. These are the opponent’s taunts, not the translator’s characterization of Jonathan.
Retain conditional trust in forces, descent to the plain, mutual contest and city troops. Measure ourselves is a contextual contest idiom rather than a literal measurement claim.

Retain the demand to learn his identity/helpers, quoted lack of foothold and fathers twice routed in their land. The change from singular addressee to plural you is natural English-neutral but recorded here.
column3: Who are the fathers and which two defeats are intended? Do not add historical identifications absent from the selected wording.

column2: Retain inability before cavalry/force, plain without stone or pebble and no refuge. The paired stone terms and emphatic terrain claim remain without geographical correction.
Retain Jonathan stirred in mind, ten thousand selected, departure from Jerusalem and Simon’s help. The emotional verb is not automatically narrowed to anger.
Retain siege of Joppa, inhabitants closing it because of Apollonius’s garrison, and attack. The final they contextually switches to the attackers rather than inhabitants attacking their own city.
column3: Would an explicit attacking subject improve clarity? The inherited pronouns remain provisional; the source itself leaves the final subject unexpressed.

column2: Retain fear, opening and Jonathan’s control of Joppa. It is naturally the city/gates in context, without specifying a gate count.

Retain three thousand cavalry, large force, apparent passage toward Azotus and movement onto the plain in confidence in cavalry. Do not supply a fully reconstructed feigned-retreat tactic as though explicitly narrated.
Retain Jonathan as the supplied contextual pursuing subject and the armies joining battle. The Greek verb has no explicit named subject in this unit.
Retain one thousand cavalry secretly left behind them. The pluperfect had left naturally explains the preceding tactical development without changing the count.
Retain awareness of ambush, encirclement and missiles from morning to evening. Missiles provisionally renders the split-wood/projectile term without claiming a precise weapon design.
column3: Should the projectile noun be more specifically darts or javelins? The broad rendering remains open to military-vocabulary review.

column2: Retain the people standing by Jonathan’s order and the enemy horses becoming weary. Enemy supplies the contextual possessive referent; the source refers to horses rather than merely dismounted riders.
Retain Simon drawing out his force, engaging the phalanx after cavalry exhaustion and routing them. The sequence distinguishes his force’s action from Jonathan’s earlier standing order.
Retain dispersed cavalry, flight to Azotus and entry into Beth-dagon, their idol shrine, for safety. The shrine’s identity is explicit and must not become a neutral unnamed fortress.
Retain Jonathan burning Azotus/towns, taking spoils and burning Dagon’s temple with those who fled into it. The human victims remain explicit and are not narrowed to an unexpressed armed subset.
Retain about eight thousand combining sword-fallen and burned people. The count is a combined total, not eight thousand in each category.
Retain departure, Ascalon encampment and inhabitants meeting him with great honour. No battle there is invented after the reception.
Retain Jonathan and companions returning with many spoils. The plural carrying expression includes the returning group without changing Jonathan’s named leadership.
Retain Alexander hearing and honouring Jonathan still more. The added honour is explicit in the repeated/continued action construction.

Propose Kinsmen of kings for the king’s Kinsmen to preserve the plural kings in the customary-gift formula. Keep golden clasp, Ekron, all its territory and inheritance; Kinsmen remains a provisional court designation, not proof of blood relation.
